summary: Root cause confirmed by live testing: every lifecycle-completion notify call site (skill_lifecycle_notify "$STATE_STATUS" in skill-base.sh's importers) passes an undefined variable -- the shared postflight contract defines the operative variable as $status, not $STATE_STATUS -- so lifecycle-notify.sh receives an empty string and silently no-ops before reaching tab resolution or TTS. The interactive needs-input path (Notification hook -> tts-notify.sh with no args) is a wholly separate, unaffected code path sharing the same tab-resolution function, which is why it correctly announced 'Tab 5' in this session while lifecycle completions never announce anything. /orchestrate is unaffected because orchestrator-postflight.sh builds its own correctly-scoped $status independently. The bug spans 12 skill files (core, web, cslib, epidemiology) plus their shared pattern-file source and predates the task-983 postflight unification by at least six weeks.

artifacts.summary: Confirms an undefined-variable bug ($STATE_STATUS vs $status) silently no-ops every lifecycle TTS/tab-color notification across 12 skill files; interactive needs-input announcements and /orchestrate are unaffected; includes live empirical reproduction and a fix and verification plan.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, WezTerm tab-number resolution for TTS notifications (get_tab_prefix() in agent-system/extensions/core/hooks/tts-notify.sh) sorts tab_id values gathered via `wezterm cli list --format=json` across ALL windows, not scoped to the current window, before computing the current tab's 1-based position. In a single-window setup this coincidentally matches the visible tab number; in a genuine multi-window setup it would not. Worth checking before trusting tab numbers reported cross-window.

When a shared @-imported context pattern file (like skill-postflight-flow.md) declares a Preconditions variable name and then a later code block in the same file references a differently-spelled variable, bash silently substitutes empty string for the unset variable rather than erroring -- this class of defect (undefined-variable name drift between a documented precondition and its own code block) is invisible to static review and was not caught for 6+ weeks across a full unification refactor (task 983) in this repo. Consider a lint that flags any bash-block variable reference with no matching assignment in its own file's Preconditions/scope section.
